question: Can an existing public resource provide a defensible external test of contextual fine-sense assignment for confirmed English phrasal-verb or verbal-idiom occurrences without conflating it with MWE detection?

task_separation.occurrence_task: Use STREUSLE 5.0 to evaluate open-text candidate retrieval, member span, gap, and VPC.full/VPC.semi/VID category.
task_separation.sense_task: Condition on a supplied multiword-verb lemma and context, then rank or select an OEWN-compatible contextual sense.
task_separation.reason: No located corpus simultaneously provides target occurrence boundaries/categories, stable fine senses, uncertainty states, rights clarity, and an adequate untouched split. Requiring one corpus for both tasks would discard valid task-specific evidence.

bounded_search.stop_rule: Inspect the actual artifacts named by the recent idiom-dataset survey and the MWE/WSD citation neighbourhoods; stop once the named English sense, idiomaticity, and verbal-MWE corpora have been classified by target construct.

candidates.evidence: The exact archive contains SemCor training data and five fixed Senseval/SemEval evaluation sets. Its XML/gold pairs include multiword verb lemmas with WordNet sense keys, but do not reliably encode all expression-member spans.

The framework projection contains 1,563 rows whose lemma type intersects a STREUSLE VPC/VID type and 74 forms with cross-occurrence sense contrasts. It is established training data, not independent held-out evidence.

The CC BY 4.0 artifact links requirement-document MWEs to WordNet 3.1/Wikipedia senses, but the paper explicitly disregards idioms, fixed expressions, light-verb constructions, and verb-particle constructions and focuses on compound nouns/proper names.
The public labels inspected are binary 0/1 idiomaticity labels plus BIO-style spans, not reusable inventory-linked contextual senses; no repository license was located.
Verb-noun combinations are labeled literal or idiomatic; they do not supply VPC/VID categories or fine senses.
The recent survey reports 78 English idiom types and 5,836 binary idiomatic/non-idiomatic instances and marks the dataset unavailable.
The task supplies binary literal/figurative decisions for ambiguous idioms rather than WordNet/OEWN fine-sense labels.
The 1,348 BNC-indexed sentences distinguish true phrasal verbs from simplex verb-preposition combinations with reported 84.5% agreement; no contextual fine sense is annotated.
The manually sense-annotated sentence corpus targets 114 selected single words; broader MASC MWE layers do not provide target VPC/VID fine-sense gold.
These resources strengthen member-span/category evidence but do not attach a stable OEWN/WordNet fine sense to each target occurrence.

The separate pinned audit found no category-confirmed VPC/VID rows, no independent annotation evidence, conflicting first-wins duplicates, and mapping loss. This does not invalidate original Senseval/SemEval gold in the WSD framework.

source_and_annotation_evidence.evidence: Raganato et al. standardize five all-words evaluation sets and distinguish them from SemCor training data; legacy sense mappings were semi-automatic with remaining cases manually checked.

Senseval-3 double-annotated verbs, nouns, and adjectives, adjudicated/corrected them with a third person, encouraged multiword constructions, allowed multiple senses and a no-fitting-sense U label, and reported 67.8% verb agreement.
SemEval-2007 Task 17 used two linguistics students who examined and resolved disagreements and reported 72% agreement for verbs.
SemEval-2015 used two taggers per language, allowed all appropriate senses, reported agreement on at least one meaning for 68% of instances, and used a third judge.
The 2025 survey inventory confirms that prominent English idiom corpora mainly expose binary idiomaticity, paraphrase, sentiment, or compositionality labels rather than inventory-linked fine senses.

framework_archive.evidence: The public project distributes the archive and its README requests citation of the framework and source tasks, but the exact zip contains no LICENSE file or explicit redistribution grant.

semcor.evidence: Use the separately audited official SemCor 3.0 distribution and retain its Princeton notice; do not infer that its grant covers every evaluation dataset in the framework.

rights.repository_policy: No source sentence, gold row, model, or external data archive is bundled in this repository. The audit stores only hashes, counts, lexical identifiers, and source links.

slice_rule: verb lemma contains an underscore in the standardized WSD XML
lemma type occurs in STREUSLE 5.0 under exactly one of V.VPC.full, V.VPC.semi, or V.VID
every gold WordNet 3.0 sense key has the same CILI ILI in OEWN 2025
the OEWN 2025 lemma has at least two candidate verb senses
decision.claim_ceiling: A feasibility-level conditional sense-ranking score on 23 externally annotated occurrences across 18 multiword-verb types, with six development rows and 17 fixed source-test rows. The source-test labels have been inspected during this artifact audit and are not a blinded project holdout. This is not validation of automatic MWE detection, member spans, VID senses, take in, ambiguity calibration, abstention, out-of-inventory handling, domain generality, or researcher usability.
critical_limits: The category link is type-level evidence imported from STREUSLE, not an occurrence-level VPC/VID judgment in the WSD texts.
The 17 source-test rows and labels were inspected during this audit; freeze them now, report the exposure, and do not call them untouched or blinded.
All 23 forms occur in SemCor and 22 rows have all gold senses represented there, so this is not a form-unseen generalization test.
The final slice contains 15 V.VPC.full types and three V.VPC.semi types but zero V.VID types.
Only find_out shows two different gold senses across evaluation occurrences.
take_in has 11 SemCor training rows and eight observed training senses but zero evaluation rows.
One row retains multiple acceptable senses; the slice does not test calibrated ambiguity, abstention, or out-of-inventory decisions.
The source tasks and annotation procedures are heterogeneous, and 23 rows are too small for stable form-level or domain-level inference.
decision.consequence_for_gate_1: The bounded search is closed. Gate 1 no longer lacks all external sense evidence, but it still lacks an adequate target-wide validation benchmark. Use the admitted slice as a smoke-test floor, retain STREUSLE as the separate occurrence benchmark, and narrow any first-paper validation claim until stronger independent evidence exists.
decision.model_authorization: Do not acquire or train BERT yet. First implement and score the transparent most-frequent-sense and gloss/rule baselines on the frozen slice; authorize at most one contextual ranker only if that tiny check exposes a ranking problem that a model can meaningfully test.

reproduction.privacy: The script reads external text locally but emits no sentences.
reproduction.command: python3 scripts/audit_wsd_mwe_sense_slice.py WSD_Evaluation_Framework.zip streusle.ud_train.v5.json streusle.ud_dev.v5.json streusle.ud_test.v5.json english-wordnet-2025-json.zip cili-pwn30-sense-map.tab cili-pwn30-ili-map.tab --check resources/wsd_mwe_sense_slice_audit_2026_09_03.json
